text:
Samir: Heads-up — customer acme-prod is seeing intermittent SSE disconnects while streaming completions (~10% of requests in last hour). Getting chunked EOFs and occasional SSL_write errors. I have a couple request IDs: req=abc123 req=def456. Need a minimal curl repro + exact headers and proxy info to escalate.

Jess: Thanks — are these hitting our hosted API or Dedicated? Also can you paste one raw request-id line from the logs?

Samir: Hosted. One log line: `2025-11-12T19:03:21Z req=abc123 status=200 stream_closed=client_eof note=\"TLS handshake resumed\" trace=tr-789`

Olivia: @Samir please try a focused curl with `--no-buffer` and force HTTP/1.1 to avoid HTTP/2 framing oddities. Include your auth header and any cookies. Example we ask customers to run:
```
# replace $TOKEN and the url
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-small\",\"prompt\":\"hello\",\"stream\":true}' \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream"
```
Add `-o /tmp/curl-output.txt` and attach that file. If they use a proxy, ask them to set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` env vars exactly the same as their app.

Samir: Ran that with `-v -N --http1.1`. curl shows HTTP/2 200 initially then immediately `* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.inference left intact` and the app reports `stream ended prematurely (chunked EOF)` after ~12s. Verbose snippet: `* SSL_write failed: error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca` — but we don't do TLS interception on our side.

Ryan: If you see `tlsv1 alert unknown ca` that usually means the client or a corporate proxy is doing MITM TLS interception or a stale CA bundle. Ask the customer to run:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.inference:443 -servername api.redwood.inference -showcerts
```
and paste the cert chain. Also try forcing `--tlsv1.2` in curl to see if that changes behaviour.

infra-bot: Deploy note: rollout 2026-02-12T03:42 completed on node gpu-8a (kernel 5.10). If customer is on older proxies, they might hit older TLS stacks.

Jess: Short checklist for the debug bundle we need from the customer before Tier2 digs in:
1) Full curl command they ran (exact flags) and the raw `curl -v -N` output file (attach).
2) One or two failing request IDs (we have abc123, def456).
3) `openssl s_client -connect` output.
4) Env (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY, http_proxy, NO_PROXY) and whether they sit behind a corporate proxy or gateway.
5) `ngrep -W byline tcp port 443` or `tcpdump -w` capture for 30s around the request (if allowed).
6) The app logs with timestamp and the `x-request-id` or our trace header if present.

Olivia: Also ask them to try removing any `Cookie:` header and re-run — we've seen cookie-based load balancer behavior cause unexpected TCP resets. If they use a long-lived token, rotate it and retry to rule out auth window issues.

Samir: I'll send the checklist to the customer and request the bundle. I'll include `x-request-id: abc123` in the curl (and note it in the support ticket) so we can correlate.

Jess: Perfect. Once they send the bundle, upload to the private ticket thread with a short summary and I'll tag @Ryan for Tier2. :thumbsup:

Samir: Bundle queued, customer running tcpdump now. Will follow up here when I have the files.

Samir: (follow-up) customer attached curl output and openssl chain — looks like intermediate cert missing on their gateway. They confirmed corporate proxy doing cert re-signing. Sending to Tier2 for guidance on mitigations (client-side CA import vs pinning).

Ryan: Thanks — will advise. If they can't import the CA, suggest using our Dedicated/private deployment with customer-provided TLS termination or allowlist the customer IPs to avoid proxy.

Samir: Closing loop with customer. Thanks everyone.
